title: A Brick Has Holes For Three Different Reasons

scenes.narration: A brick has holes punched straight through the middle, which is an odd thing to do to an object whose whole job is being solid.
scenes.note: The paradox up front: an object whose job is being solid, full of holes.

beats.action: Bill holds up a brick; three holes run through it
camera punches through one hole and out the other side
a SOLID? label lands over the brick and wavers
Bill turns the brick end over end, looking through the holes

scenes.narration: Mortar squeezes down into them and sets there, so each brick is keyed into the one above rather than glued along a flat face.
scenes.note: Reason one. The keying action is the good visual — mortar as a plug, not a glue line.

mortar presses down into the holes and sets, forming plugs
the plugs lock the courses together; a flat-glued wall beside it slides apart

scenes.narration: Wet clay also has to dry and fire without cracking, and heat reaches the middle of a perforated brick far faster than a solid lump.
scenes.note: Reason two. Heat reaching the middle — a heat map, two bricks compared.

beats.action: a solid brick and a perforated brick enter a kiln side by side
the solid brick heats unevenly and cracks through the middle
heat travels through the perforated brick from inside and out; it fires evenly
the kiln door closes over both bricks

beats.action: heat builds in the kiln; both bricks glow at the edges

scenes.narration: Less clay, less fuel, lighter to lift, stronger wall.
